In a lengthy interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses recent changes to the company's ChatGPT desktop app and outlines plans to eventually eliminate the tabbed interface. Watch below.

Work could eventually function seamlessly within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Stern offered a preview of her upcoming interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her brand-new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern dropped the full interview, which covers a wide range of topics, including the new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware development plans, the Apple lawsuit, and the recent Hugging Face hack.

During the interview, Stern noted that OpenAI recently decided to merge its ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, while simultaneously launching a new agentic mode for ChatGPT called Work.

The merged interface has confused users, particularly those who simply want to continue using ChatGPT but are struggling to locate their conversations.

OpenAI has since updated the app to include separate tabs for Work and ChatGPT at the top of the interface, along with a dropdown menu in the sidebar for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is slightly easier to navigate, the overall interface remains somewhat convoluted.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern, admitting the new interface is "indeed a bit messy," but added that it represents a "gradual step" toward the future, where the Work tab will disappear and its functionality will be "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also noted that despite the confusion surrounding the launch of the merged app, OpenAI is seeing the desired results, with Codex's user base doubling from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.
